arc.scene1_hook: A figure holds a yardstick, measuring everything — career, relationships, achievements. Each measurement produces a number that floats up and turns to ash. The figure, exhausted, snaps the yardstick over their knee. CRACK. The pieces fall. Relief washes over their face. They sit down, free at last. But the camera slowly pulls back to reveal: the broken yardstick pieces still surround them, forming a cage. Title pill: "STILL A PRISON".
arc.scene2_mystery: The figure sits inside the cage of broken yardstick pieces, arms crossed, defiant. Outside the cage, other figures rush past holding their own yardsticks — measuring, comparing, climbing. The caged figure looks superior, enlightened. A "FREEDOM" label glows above them. The nihilist's refusal to measure feels like liberation. It looks like the only honest response to a rigged system. If the yardstick lies, why keep using it?
arc.scene3_wrong_answer: The assumption: refusing to measure is freedom. The yardstick pieces lie on the ground, crossed out with a red X. A weight lifts off the figure's shoulders — animated as a literal heavy block floating away. The figure stands tall, unburdened. "NOTHING MATTERS" text in clean white. It's not laziness or despair — it's the recognition that a rigged yardstick produces meaningless measurements. Setting it down feels like setting down something enormously heavy you didn't realize you were carrying.
arc.scene4_contradiction: But the figure who set down the yardstick is still facing the direction it pointed. They haven't moved. A ghost outline of the yardstick appears — translucent, hovering where it was. The figure who "rejected success" is still defined by success — oriented by the very concept they abandoned. An orbit path draws around the trophy they rejected: they're circling it, not walking away from it. The "FREEDOM" label flickers and rewrites: "FREEDOM'S SHADOW." Reaction is not freedom.
arc.scene5_proof: Split screen. Left: a figure actively climbing (holding yardstick, measuring). Right: a figure sitting still (broken yardstick, arms crossed). Draw a dotted line connecting them both to the same central point — the SUCCESS trophy. One chases it. One refuses it. Both are defined by it. A pendulum swings between "PURSUE" and "REFUSE" — but the fulcrum never moves. Below: "The nihilist clears the field but plants nothing. Tells you what to stop doing but not what to do instead." The life hollows out — the figure on the right slowly fades to translucent.
arc.scene6_betrayal: The nihilist's cage dissolves — not because they escaped, but because they realize it was never a cage. The broken pieces of yardstick reassemble into a question mark. The real trap wasn't the measurement. The real trap was thinking that rejecting the measurement was an answer. Negation is not a destination. You can live there, but the life hollows out. The figure stands in an empty field — free from metrics, yes, but also free from meaning. The emptiest kind of liberty.

tts_script: If success is imposed, if its metrics are inherited, if its architecture serves power — then what are we chasing? The nihilist does the only honest thing: refuses to measure at all. This is not laziness. It's the recognition that a rigged yardstick produces meaningless measurements. There is a freedom in this refusal that's difficult to communicate to anyone still holding the yardstick. From outside, it looks like giving up. From inside, it feels like setting down something enormously heavy you didn't realize you were carrying. But nihilism clears the field and plants nothing. You can't live in negation forever. The nihilist who merely refuses is still defined by the thing refused. Reaction is not freedom. It is freedom's shadow.
